summary: Setup is easy: a new app can be installed in its development workspace right away, and any workspace can install it once App Distribution is enabled, with no Slack review required. The main thing that can hold up launch is that workspace owners can require app approval before members install it. Unlisted apps also get lower rate limits on conversations.history and conversations.replies.
handoff: An agent can choose the scopes and build the authorize link; you create the app, click through the console, copy the client secret and connect your own workspace.

gates.title: New apps install only in the development workspace until distribution is enabled
gates.what: Until you set a Redirect URL and enable App Distribution, the app can only be installed in its development workspace.
gates.where: api.slack.com/apps → your app → Settings → Manage Distribution (developer)
gates.todo: Add the Redirect URL, then follow the Manage Distribution instructions to enable distribution.

gates.title: No Slack review is needed to connect users
Workspace owners can require approval before members install your app
gates.what: With app approval enabled, members can only install pre-approved apps. Owners can restrict apps so they cannot be installed or requested.
gates.where: Slack Admin → Apps and workflows → App management settings → Require approved apps (workspace owner)
gates.todo: Tell customers their workspace owner may need to pre-approve the app.

gates.title: No recurring re-verification mentioned for unlisted apps

requirements.text: A Slack account and a workspace where you can create and install the app
A public HTTPS URL on your server to receive the OAuth redirect
A server able to exchange the code for a token using the client secret

steps.text: api.slack.com/apps: sign in and click Create New App to create the app in your development workspace
steps.detail: Pick the workspace you will use for testing.

steps.text: Features → OAuth & Permissions → Scopes: add the bot scopes (and user scopes only if you must act as a user) the features need
steps.detail: Scopes requested in the authorize URL must be ones configured here.

steps.text: Features → OAuth & Permissions → Redirect URLs: add your HTTPS callback URL and click Save URLs
steps.detail: The redirect_uri you send must match or be a subdirectory of a saved URL; no # anchors.

steps.text: Settings → Manage Distribution: follow the instructions to enable App Distribution
steps.why: Without it the app installs only in the development workspace.

steps.text: Settings → Basic Information → App Credentials: copy the Client ID and Client Secret
Build the authorize link from your client ID, bot scopes and redirect URL
steps.detail: Bot scopes go in scope=…; user scopes, if any, go in user_scope=….

steps.text: Browser: open your app’s Slack authorize link and click Allow to connect your own workspace
steps.detail: The link is https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize?client_id=…&scope=…&redirect_uri=… with your client ID, bot scopes and redirect URL filled in.

steps.text: Your redirect endpoint: take the code from the redirect and call oauth.v2.access with code, client_id and client_secret to get the access token
steps.detail: The code expires after ten minutes; send the same redirect_uri if you used one in the authorize step.

blockers.problem: bad_redirect_uri error during the token exchange
blockers.fix: When multiple Redirect URLs are configured, send the same redirect_uri in both the authorize and oauth.v2.access calls.

blockers.problem: invalid_team_for_non_distributed_app: the app cannot be installed on another workspace
blockers.fix: Enable App Distribution in Manage Distribution before sending users from other workspaces.

blockers.problem: Unlisted apps get low rate limits on conversations.history and conversations.replies (1 request per minute, 15 objects per request) for new installs
blockers.fix: Avoid these methods for new installs, use the Events API instead, or pursue Marketplace approval if distributing commercially.

blockers.problem: A workspace with app approval on blocks member installs
blockers.fix: Ask the workspace owner to approve the app.

couldNotVerify: Whether a paid Slack plan is needed for customers to use the app in production.
Whether Slack applies any ongoing re-verification to unlisted apps.

claims.statement: A newly created app can only be installed in its development workspace until a Redirect URL is set and App Distribution is enabled.
claims.quote: A newly created Slack app can only be installed in its development workspace in the beginning. By setting an OAuth Redirect URL and enabling App Distribution , the app becomes to be ready for installation in other workspaces.

claims.statement: OAuth allows a user in any Slack workspace to install the app.
claims.sourceTitle: Installing via OAuth authorization code flow | Slack Developer Docs
claims.quote: OAuth allows a user in any Slack workspace to install your app.

claims.statement: New non-Marketplace commercially distributed apps are limited to 1 request per minute and 15 objects per request on conversations.history and conversations.replies.
claims.sourceTitle: Rate limit changes for non-Marketplace apps | Slack Developer Docs
claims.quote: The new rate limits will be updated to allow 1 request per minute and will return a maximum of 15 objects per request.
claims.note: [Check: the quote only partly supports this. Quote gives the new limit of 1 request per minute and 15 objects per request, but does not specify that it applies to non-Marketplace commercially distributed apps or name conversations.history and conversations.replies.]

claims.statement: Workspace owners can enable app approval to pre-approve or restrict apps; by default members can install without approval.
claims.sourceTitle: Manage app approval for your workspace | Slack
claims.quote: Apps connect third-party services to Slack, and by default, members can install them without approval from a workspace owner. If they like, workspace owners can enable app approval to pre-approve or restrict certain apps for their workspace.

claims.statement: With app approval enabled, members cannot install or request restricted apps.
claims.sourceTitle: Manage app approval for your workspace | Slack
claims.quote: When app approval has been enabled, members can install and start using pre-approved apps straight away. They cannot install or request any apps that you choose to restrict.

claims.statement: The redirect_uri and configured Redirect URL must use HTTPS.
claims.sourceTitle: Installing via OAuth authorization code flow | Slack Developer Docs
claims.quote: The redirect_uri must use HTTPS. Alternatively, you can configure a Redirect URL in the App Management page under OAuth & Permissions . A Redirect URL must also use HTTPS.
claims.note: [Re-quoted automatically: the first quote didn't state this.]

claims.statement: The temporary code is exchanged for a token by calling oauth.v2.access with the client secret; the code expires after ten minutes.
claims.sourceTitle: Installing via OAuth authorization code flow | Slack Developer Docs
claims.quote: That's your temporary authorization code, which expires after ten minutes.
claims.note: [Check: the quote only partly supports this. Quote says the temporary code expires after ten minutes, but does not mention exchanging it via oauth.v2.access or using the client secret.]

claims.statement: Bot scopes use the scope parameter and user scopes use user_scope.
claims.sourceTitle: Installing via OAuth authorization code flow | Slack Developer Docs
claims.quote: Bot scopes should be added as scope=<bot_scope> , and user scopes should be added as user_scope=<user_scope> .

claims.statement: With multiple Redirect URLs, redirect_uri must be sent in both authorize and access steps with the same value or bad_redirect_uri occurs.
claims.sourceTitle: Installing via OAuth authorization code flow | Slack Developer Docs
claims.quote: When there are multiple Redirect URL values configured, the redirect_url parameter must be sent in both the Authorize and Access steps described below, and the parameter value must be the same for both steps — otherwise, you will encounter a bad_redirect_uri error:
claims.note: [Re-quoted automatically: the first quote didn't state this.]

claims.statement: No Slack review requirement for connecting users via OAuth is mentioned on the OAuth install page.
claims.sourceTitle: Installing via OAuth authorization code flow | Slack Developer Docs
claims.note: No review is mentioned in Installing via OAuth authorization code flow; Marketplace review appears to be optional.

claims.statement: No yearly re-verification or audit is mentioned in the Marketplace review guide.
claims.sourceTitle: Slack Marketplace review process | Slack Developer Docs
claims.note: No such requirement is mentioned in Slack Marketplace review process.

claims.statement: Client ID and Client Secret are under Settings > Basic Information > App Credentials.
claims.quote: SLACK_CLIENT_ID OAuth 2.0 Client ID (Find at Settings > Basic Information > App Credentials ) SLACK_CLIENT_SECRET OAuth 2.0 Client Secret (Find at Settings > Basic Information > App Credentials )
claims.note: [Re-quoted automatically: the first quote didn't state this.]

claims.statement: Users are redirected to https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize to request scopes.
claims.sourceTitle: Installing via OAuth authorization code flow | Slack Developer Docs
claims.quote: To request scopes, redirect Slack users to https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize .

claims.statement: SIWS user scopes cannot be combined with non-SIWS scopes in one OAuth flow.
claims.sourceTitle: Installing via OAuth authorization code flow | Slack Developer Docs
claims.quote: invalid_scope : Occurs if requesting a non-existent scope or requesting a set of scopes that are in conflict with each other (e.g. SIWS user scopes cannot be combined with non-SIWS user scopes).
claims.note: [Re-quoted automatically: the first quote didn't state this.]

claims.statement: If redirect_uri was sent in the first step, the same value must be sent in the access step.
claims.sourceTitle: Installing via OAuth authorization code flow | Slack Developer Docs
claims.quote: If you sent a redirect_uri field in the first step, you must send that same field with the same value in this step.

claims.statement: invalid_team_for_non_distributed_app occurs when authorizing an undistributed app on a team where it was not created.
claims.sourceTitle: Installing via OAuth authorization code flow | Slack Developer Docs
claims.quote: invalid_team_for_non_distributed_app : Occurs when attempting to install/authorize an undistributed Slack API app on a team where the app was not created.
